cardSummary: New subdivisions, hillside lots and townhouse sites, often on thin soil over rock or fill, with permit areas near slopes and lakes.
intro: Langford has a lot of new building: subdivisions in Westhills and Happy Valley, hillside homes on Bear Mountain, townhouse stratas, and retail centres along the main corridors. Many yards here start from bare ground.

Langford’s Tree Protection Bylaw applies across the city, and tree and vegetation removal is also regulated in development permit areas such as steep slopes, sensitive ecosystems and land near lakes and streams. See [commercial and contractor work](/commercial/) or [get a free quote](/free-quote/?area=langford).
localRulesIntro: In Langford, the questions are whether a tree is protected and whether the lot falls in a development permit area. Boulevard and public-land trees are a separate matter for the City’s Parks department.

localNotes.title: Langford Tree Protection Bylaw
localNotes.text: Langford's Tree Protection Bylaw applies across the city. Removing a protected tree on private property needs a Tree Permit (or a Development Permit when part of development); work in designated development permit areas is also regulated, and Parks authorizes all removals on public land and boulevards.

localNotes.title: CRD lawn-watering schedule
localNotes.text: CRD Stage 1 watering rules run May 1 to September 30 for properties on the regional water supply: lawns may be watered on Wednesdays and Saturdays (even addresses) or Thursdays and Sundays (odd addresses), 4-10 am or 7-10 pm; hand watering and drip irrigation of trees, shrubs and gardens is allowed any day. Multi-unit complexes use the complex's street address. New sod or seed does not need a permit and has a temporary schedule.

localNotes.title: Invasive plants and disposal
localNotes.text: The CRD Regional Invasive Species Program lists priority species (including giant hogweed, knotweed, gorse, poison hemlock, shiny geranium and yellow toadflax) and asks for sightings to be reported. Invasive plants must be disposed of properly: Hartland Landfill takes them bagged and labelled or in covered loads, and knotweed needs a controlled waste permit and is not accepted at municipal yard-waste drop-offs.

conditions.title: Thin soil on new lots
conditions.body: New-build yards often have a thin layer of topsoil over compacted fill or blasted rock. Checking soil depth before sod or planting goes in saves a lawn that browns out in its first summer.

conditions.title: Slopes and rock on Bear Mountain
conditions.body: Hillside lots are steep and rocky. Retaining walls, drainage and erosion control usually come before planting, and some slopes sit inside development permit areas.

conditions.title: Lakes and streams
conditions.body: Homes near Langford Lake, Florence Lake and Glen Lake may fall under the development permit rules for land near water, so clearing near the shore needs a check.

conditions.title: New lawns and watering
conditions.body: Most subdivisions are on the regional supply. New sod or seed does not need a CRD permit and has its own temporary schedule before the regular lawn days apply.

topServices.why: Bare new-build yards and contractor sites need grading, soil, sod and planting installed to plan.
Young planting at new stratas and homes needs regular care for its first few seasons to establish.

servicesBlurb.landscape-installation: New-build landscaping for homeowners and general contractors, from grading to sod.
servicesBlurb.irrigation: Irrigation for new lawns and retail planters, set to CRD watering days.
servicesBlurb.tree-vegetation: Tree work on hillside and lakeside lots, with permit areas checked first.

jobNotes.title: New-sod schedule after handover
jobNotes.body: A controller was set to the CRD new-sod schedule after a builder’s handover, then moved back to the regular odd-address lawn days once the sod had rooted.

jobNotes.title: Bare slope behind a townhouse block
jobNotes.body: A bare cut slope behind a townhouse block was planted with groundcover and mulched to slow runoff onto the parking area.

cta.heading: Get a free quote in Langford
cta.body: Tell us whether the yard is new or established, and if you are a builder, send the landscape drawings. Slopes and nearby lakes help us check the permit side early.
